title: Unauthenticated MCP key management on the local bridge
description: The security middleware authenticates only paths equal to /mcp or starting with /mcp/. The key-management routes /api/mcp/keys (GET), /api/mcp/keys (POST) and /api/mcp/keys/{key_id} (DELETE) are registered on the FastAPI app and therefore sit outside that branch, so a caller with no credential can list active key metadata, mint a new MCP API key, and revoke an existing key by id.
claimed_root_cause: The authentication branch of security_and_rate_limit_middleware matches only /mcp and /mcp/* paths, while the key-management routes live under /api/mcp/keys.

trace.description: Route handler create_mcp_key is registered on the FastAPI app and requires no credential.
The middleware authenticates only when path == '/mcp' or path.startswith('/mcp/'), so '/api/mcp/keys' skips the check entirely.
The handler mints a 192-bit token, appends its SHA-256 hash to artifacts/cache/mcp_api_keys.json and returns the raw token once.

evidence.description: Authentication condition covers only '/mcp' and '/mcp/'.
GET /api/mcp/keys lists non-revoked key metadata and the tool catalog.
DELETE /api/mcp/keys/{key_id} revokes by id and distinguishes unknown ids with 404.
The raw MCP token is returned in the create response.

blockers: Runtime execution environment unavailable: no Python dependency stack (fastapi, mcp, torch, rdkit) installed on host; target-controlled code cannot be executed, preventing direct observation of unauthorized route access.

Deployment model constraint: architecture.md§3 calibrates severity to local-loopback deployment (127.0.0.1 bind per README.md); candidates depending on public bind, tunnel, or shared multi-user host are kept as needs_validation rather than confirmed.

validation_plan.local: Source code inspection confirms that security_and_rate_limit_middleware at api/server.py:187 only authenticates paths matching '/mcp' or '/mcp/*', while the key-management routes /api/mcp/keys (GET/POST/DELETE) are outside this branch. No other source-visible control authenticates these routes.
validation_plan.deployment: Per architecture.md§3, the default deployment binds the FastAPI bridge to 127.0.0.1. Demonstrating unauthorized remote access requires a public bind address, tunnel, or shared multi-user host configuration, which falls outside the local-loopback severity calibration.

title: Unverified third-party dataset downloads shape published results
description: The data pipeline downloads DAVIS and DrugBank DDI data from fixed HTTPS URLs and writes the response bytes straight to disk with no checksum or schema validation; the downloaded data flows into the clean CSV artifacts that feed the precomputed screening results served by the studio.
claimed_root_cause: Third-party data is trusted after transfer without any independent integrity check, so the trust root for published screening results is the upstream mirror itself.

trace.description: requests.get over HTTPS retrieves the DAVIS data set from a fixed Dataverse URL.
The response bytes are written to disk without checksum or schema validation.
The unverified data is parsed and written into the clean CSV artifact that feeds the pipeline.

evidence.description: Fixed-URL download without integrity verification.
The DrugBank DDI download follows the same pattern.

blockers: Cannot observe runtime TLS behavior or actual data content from source alone to verify integrity of downloaded bytes against upstream mirrors.
Cannot confirm from source whether published web/public/data artifacts in a given deployment were produced from these specific downloads or whether the upstream mirrors are the canonical ones.

validation_plan.local: Reproduce the download functions with a harmless fixture URL and verify that response bytes are written without checksum/schema validation. Use a mock server returning known content and confirm no integrity check is performed before writing.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner observation needed: confirm whether the published web/public/data artifacts were produced from these downloads, verify the upstream Harvard Dataverse and S3 mirrors are the canonical sources, and check if any deployment-level checksum or manifest exists (e.g., artifacts/run_manifest.json).

title: Loopback MCP endpoint with DNS-rebinding protection disabled
description: The Streamable HTTP MCP transport is created with TransportSecuritySettings(enable_dns_rebinding_protection=False), so the MCP server performs no Host-header validation for its HTTP transport. The transport's own origin binding is therefore replaced by the bridge's API-key middleware, and the middleware's own CORS allow-list does not constrain non-browser clients.
claimed_root_cause: The HTTP MCP transport is constructed with DNS-rebinding protection explicitly disabled, so a browser page on another origin can address the loopback MCP endpoint once it holds a valid key, and the transport performs no Host check of its own.

trace.description: TransportSecuritySettings(enable_dns_rebinding_protection=False) is passed to FastMCP for the stateless HTTP transport.
The bridge's own credential check applies to /mcp paths; the CORS middleware answers browser preflights but does not restrict non-browser clients.
All six tools are registered on the same FastMCP instance and are reachable by any caller that satisfies the bridge's key check.

evidence.description: Source comment states that the localhost-only Host-header lock is disabled to allow tunneled clients.
CORS allow-list is built from API_ALLOWED_ORIGINS with a localhost default.
The MCP sub-application is mounted at '/' on the same FastAPI app.

blockers: The mcp package source is not installed in this environment, so the exact Host/Origin behaviour of TransportSecuritySettings(enable_dns_rebinding_protection=False) cannot be observed at runtime.

The bridge deployment configuration (uvicorn --host address) determines whether the loopback MCP endpoint is accessible from non-loopback origins, which decides if the disabled DNS-rebinding protection is exploitable.

validation_plan.local: When the mcp package is available, read the TransportSecuritySettings source to verify the exact Host header validation behavior enabled by enable_dns_rebinding_protection=False and enable_dns_rebinding_protection=True.
validation_plan.deployment: Verify the bridge deployment configuration (uvicorn --host address) to confirm whether the MCP endpoint is bound to 127.0.0.1 or a public address, which decides if the disabled DNS-rebinding protection is exploitable.

title: Raw MCP key rendered in the DOM and copied to the clipboard
description: After an operator creates an MCP key through the studio UI, the raw token is held in React state, rendered into the DOM, embedded in a copyable JSON client configuration and written to the system clipboard. It is not written to localStorage or logged.
claimed_root_cause: The reveal-once key is exposed to every script running in the studio origin and to the system clipboard history, so any same-origin script execution would obtain it.

trace.description: The create response's api_key is stored in component state.
document.execCommand('copy') copies the selected text to the system clipboard from a temporary DOM textarea.
The raw token is rendered into the studio DOM.

evidence.description: The raw key is displayed to the operator.
The execCommand fallback puts the secret into a temporary textarea in the DOM.

reason: The MCP key is revealed to the operator who created it as intentional UI behavior; the concern about same-origin script execution only applies in a different threat model (e.g., XSS on a shared origin), not in the single-operator local-loopback deployment. No lower-trust principal or concrete reachable result is established against the operator's interest.

title: Unlocked key store can lose a revocation or resurrect a revoked key
description: MCPKeyStore documents itself as thread-safe, but create_key, revoke_key and verify_key all perform an unlocked read-modify-write of the shared JSON store, and verify_key rewrites the whole record list on every successful verification.
claimed_root_cause: No lock protects the read-modify-write cycle in MCPKeyStore, while verify_key writes the entire record list back on each successful verification.

trace.description: A successful verification reads the records, updates last_used_at_utc and writes the full list back.
The record list is read from disk without any lock, so a concurrent writer's change is not visible.
The stale list is written back with os.replace, overwriting a concurrent revocation.

evidence.description: The class docstring claims thread safety.
revoke_key reads, mutates and writes the same file with no lock.
verify_key rewrites the records on every successful verification.

blockers: Whether the lost-update interleaving that resurrects a revoked key is reachable depends on the ASGI server's concurrency model for synchronous endpoints
The single-operator local-loopback deployment model calibrated in architecture.md differs from shared or public-facing deployment contexts

validation_plan.local: Source code inspection confirms the unlocked read-modify-write pattern in api/mcp_keys.py. The race condition is visible in create_key (line 75-77), revoke_key (line 104-113), and verify_key (line 127-140) without any locking mechanism.
validation_plan.deployment: Whether concurrent requests can interleave depends on the ASGI server's thread pool scheduling for synchronous FastAPI endpoints. Runtime testing against a running server would be needed to observe the interleaving in practice.

title: Root-mounted MCP sub-application may register routes outside the authenticated /mcp path
description: The bridge authenticates only paths equal to /mcp or starting with /mcp/. The MCP Streamable HTTP sub-application is built by the installed mcp package (streamable_http_path='/mcp') and is mounted at the root of the FastAPI app, so any path the package registers outside /mcp would be handled without any credential check. The package source is not present in this environment, so the mounted application's route table cannot be enumerated from repository source.
claimed_root_cause: The bridge's authentication branch is path-based, while the MCP sub-application is mounted at '/', so any route the package registers outside '/mcp' would bypass the credential check entirely.

trace.description: The MCP Streamable HTTP sub-application is mounted at the root of the FastAPI app.
The credential check runs only for paths == '/mcp' or starting with '/mcp/'.
All six tools are registered on the FastMCP instance whose HTTP app is mounted at '/', so a handler reachable outside '/mcp' would run without a credential.

evidence.description: _MCP_HTTP_APP is created by _MCP_HTTP_SERVER.streamable_http_app() from the mcp package.
Authentication condition covers only '/mcp' and '/mcp/'.
The HTTP transport is created with DNS-rebinding protection disabled.

blockers: The installed mcp package source is not available in this environment, so the route table registered by FastMCP.streamable_http_app() cannot be enumerated from source; whether it registers any path outside '/mcp' is unknown.

validation_plan.local: Owner-observed inspection of the installed FastMCP streamable_http_app route table on the operator's own machine (e.g., reading the registered routes from the installed mcp package pip install), without sending traffic to a running deployment.
validation_plan.deployment: Read the installed FastMCP streamable_http_app route table on the operator's machine to determine which paths the mounted MCP sub-application registers; compare against the middleware's authentication branch.

title: Loopback rate-limit bucket is shared by every local caller
description: The inference routes are protected by a per-client-IP rate limit of 30 requests per minute, but the bucket key is request.client.host. On the documented loopback deployment every caller shares 127.0.0.1, so a single local caller can consume the operator's own allowance and make the operator's own inference requests fail with HTTP 429.
claimed_root_cause: The rate limiter buckets requests by client IP, and on a loopback deployment every local process maps to the same 127.0.0.1 bucket, so the control cannot distinguish the operator from another local caller.

trace.description: The inference routes are reachable without a credential and are counted against the shared client-IP bucket.
The bucket key is request.client.host, which is 127.0.0.1 for every local caller on a loopback deployment.
Once the bucket holds 30 entries the middleware answers 429 for every further request from that client, including the operator's own.

evidence.description: RATE_LIMITED_PREFIXES covers /api/predict and /api/mix only.
The bucket key is request.client.host.
The limit is enforced against the bucket before the handler runs.

reason: The only effect is that the operator's own requests can be rate-limited to HTTP 429 when another local caller (e.g., another browser tab or CLI process) exhausts the shared 127.0.0.1 bucket. No principal other than the operator is affected; this is self-limiting in the single-operator local-loopback deployment model per architecture.md§3.

title: Absolute model path disclosed in 503 error detail
description: POST /api/predict and POST /api/mix convert FileNotFoundError into HTTPException(status_code=503, detail=str(exc)), so a missing model checkpoint returns the absolute filesystem path of the checkpoint to any unauthenticated caller.
claimed_root_cause: The error path passes the raw exception text into the HTTP response detail instead of a generic message.

trace.description: Any caller can post a custom molecule and protein pair; the route requires no credential.
FileNotFoundError is caught and its text becomes the response detail.
The 503 response body carries the absolute checkpoint path.

evidence.description: except FileNotFoundError as exc: raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail=str(exc)) from exc.
The mix route repeats the same pattern.
MODELS_DIR resolves the checkpoint path that appears in the message.

blockers: no OS-enforced sandbox available on Windows host
Python dependency stack (fastapi, torch, rdkit, mcp) not installed; runtime validation impossible in this environment

validation_plan.local: Verify source code at api/server.py lines 268-269 and 286-287 show FileNotFoundError detail leaked as HTTP 503 response detail; confirm MODELS_DIR at ml/config.py line 19 defines model path base
validation_plan.deployment: Python runtime and dependencies unavailable; runtime reproduction cannot be performed. Candidate calibrated to local-loopback deployment per architecture.md §2.

title: Unvalidated shared-link fields persisted to localStorage
description: Hash-derived fields are applied to the studio session and persisted to browser storage without validation against the application's own data model.
claimed_root_cause: Hash-derived fields are applied to the studio session and persisted to browser storage without validation against the application's own data model.

trace.description: Hash parameters are parsed into a partial session; stage, quickChip and sortOrder are allow-listed but targetId, drugId, searchQuery and minPkd are not.
The parsed session is merged into the studio state.
The merged session is written to localStorage under the session key.

evidence.description: targetId is taken verbatim from the hash.
searchQuery is taken verbatim from the hash.
The session is persisted to localStorage.

reason: The primary impact is self-inflicted view changes in a single-operator local deployment. Per client-side validation rules (CLIENT-SIDE.md core discipline: The impact must reach a victim's session, another origin, or shared persistence. Self-injection and disclosure of the attacker's own data are not findings.), and architecture.md section 3 calibration to loopback deployment, no cross-principal boundary violation is source-visible. URL hash parameters are parsed and merged into studio state, then persisted to origin-scoped localStorage. The studio validates targetId/drugId against loaded candidates, but the overall effect is limited to the same principal's session within a single browser context.

title: API-provided SVG inserted as HTML in the studio origin
description: The studio inserts the API response SVG through dangerouslySetInnerHTML in CustomPredictModal.tsx and MixLabStage.tsx. The string is generated by RDKit from the canonicalized molecule, so caller-supplied SMILES does not carry markup into it; the remaining question is which principal controls the API response the studio trusts, given that API_BASE_URL comes from NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL without origin validation.
claimed_root_cause: The studio renders an API response body as HTML with no sanitization layer, and the API origin is taken from NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL without validation, so the trust boundary is the API host rather than the SVG content itself.

trace.description: The API origin is taken from NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL with a loopback default and no origin validation.
The response body is returned to the component as-is.
The API-provided SVG string is inserted into the studio origin as HTML.

evidence.description: dangerouslySetInnerHTML with the API SVG markup.
The second insertion point for the online-drug SVG.
The SVG is produced by RDKit MolDraw2DSVG from the canonicalized molecule.
The server renders the SVG with render_attributed_2d_svg and returns it in the response.

reason: The RDKit SVG renderer (ml/chem_filters.py render_2d_svg, ml/explain.py render_attributed_2d_svg) produces structural-only SVG markup from canonicalized SMILES. Element symbols (C, N, O, etc.) in the output are intrinsic chemical properties derived from atomic numbers, not attacker-controlled text. No path exists for caller-supplied SMILES data to reach the SVG as script-carrying markup, refuting the XSS claim. The 'no sanitization' concern is moot since the markup itself is inherently script-safe; the actual issue is an API origin trust boundary, not a cross-site scripting vulnerability.
